name: PCF8574 / PCF8574A I2C I/O expander
description: 8-bit quasi-bidirectional I/O expander on I2C (NXP PCF8574, address 0x20 + A2..A0; PCF8574A 0x38): a written 1 is a weak pull-up the pin can read through, with a strong pull-up during the acknowledge; a 0 a strong low; reads return the pin levels; INT_N goes low when a pin changes. The chip on the common I2C LCD backpacks (0x27).

pins.name: A0
pins.doc: Address bit 0: high adds it to the address (tie it; unconnected reads low)

pins.name: A1
pins.doc: Address bit 1: high adds it to the address (tie it; unconnected reads low)

pins.name: A2
pins.doc: Address bit 2: high adds it to the address (tie it; unconnected reads low)

pins.name: INT_N
pins.doc: Interrupt, open drain, active low: a pin changed since the last read or write

pins.name: VCC
pins.doc: Supply, 2.5 to 6 V (defaults to the family rail)

variant.doc: The part: PCF8574 answers at 0x20 + A2..A0, PCF8574A at 0x38 + A2..A0

functional.claims: Address from A0..A2 (and the variant), quasi-bidirectional ports (weak 1, strong 0) updated at the acknowledge, reads of the pin levels, INT_N on a change and cleared by a read or write; no answer below 2.5 V.
omissions: the supply current and output current limits (the 100 uA source and 25 mA sink are drive strengths)
an unconnected A0..A2 reads low (the datasheet wants them tied)
the 400 kHz bus limit (faster clocks are decoded too)

timed.claims: As functional, with the strong pull-up during the acknowledge clock's high time and INT_N's 4 us delays.
omissions: the supply current and output current limits (the 100 uA source and 25 mA sink are drive strengths)
an unconnected A0..A2 reads low (the datasheet wants them tied)
the 400 kHz bus limit (faster clocks are decoded too)

electrical.claims: Pins bridge to analog nets with the family's pin-model defaults; the behaviour is the Lua model's.
omissions: the supply current and output current limits (the 100 uA source and 25 mA sink are drive strengths)
an unconnected A0..A2 reads low (the datasheet wants them tied)
the 400 kHz bus limit (faster clocks are decoded too)
